evidence_items.publisher: Nature, official full-text copy supplied by Europe PMC
evidence_items.explanation: The paper combines a neural language model with symbolic deduction and reports 25 of 30 problems solved, compared with 10 for the previous state of the art and 18 for its strongest enhanced baseline. The work was accepted in 2023 and publicly published in January 2024.

evidence_items.publisher: ICLR 2019 authors, paper hosted on arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 4.2, Data-efficient and interpretable visual reasoning
evidence_items.explanation: NS-CL combines neural perception and parsing with explicit symbolic program execution, and reports competitive visual-reasoning performance with superior data efficiency. Its authors include MIT, Tsinghua and MIT-IBM researchers as well as DeepMind, supporting the reference to achievements involving others.
